entry.name: Attribute prefix
entry.source: reading 47 (an xsi: attribute is exported byte for byte, C54), with https://www.w3.org/TR/xml-names/#ns-decl (Namespaces in XML 1.0 §3: 'The prefix xml is by definition bound to the namespace name http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace … Other prefixes MUST NOT be bound to this namespace name'; 'The prefix xmlns is used only to declare namespace bindings') and https://www.w3.org/TR/xml-names/#defaulting (§6.2: 'The namespace name for an unprefixed attribute name always has no value'): every attribute keeps the prefix its name is written with, empty for a name in no namespace, xml for the XML namespace's, and neither empty, xml nor xmlns for an xsi:, xlink: or namespaced open name (attributes.ts Attribute_prefix)

entry.name: Manifest overlay
entry.source: plan §1.6 and the W5 amendment's C18, under decision S3: each manifest overlay (ResourceHref, File) is its element's row, keyed by its node, and holds its own facts alone: it stands at a node of its kind (a constant pin) exactly where its href is written and holds its resolution, never its form, each header with exactly the arm its scope names (grizzle's alternatives: ResourceHrefPath and FilePath an entry path in the package, ResourceHrefOutside and FileOutside a path outside it, as written), and a file's resource is its node's parent, which its laws read through Node; the manifest's identifier is its attribute's value (overlay-queries/package.ts manifestIdentifiers), one per package by the single root N5 admits (Q5.06)

entry.source: reading 121: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DataCharacteristic_Equal.Attr_tolerance (§5.46.2: 'If the tolerance mode is absolute or relative then the tolerance must be specified. The tolerance consists of two positive numbers, t0 and t1, that define the lower and upper bounds. If only one value is given it is used for both') and #DataModel_ToleranceList (§9.1.5: 'a space separated list of either strings (must not contain a space) or numbers'): a qti-equal whose tolerance-mode is absolute or relative writes tolerance, every tolerance holds one or two values, and each value in xs:double's lexical space is above 0, a string naming a variable read at run time (operators.ts Tolerance, toleranceRequired, Equal_tolerance)

entry.source: reading 104: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DataCharacteristic_SimpleChoice.Attr_identifier (§5.132.1, and §5.7.1, §5.55.1, §5.56.1, §5.58.1, §5.65.1, §5.67.1, §5.73.1 and §5.131.1: 'This identifier must not be used by any other choice or item variable', five classes naming their own noun) and https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Derived_Identifier (§7.16: an identifier is 'a logical reference to another object in the item, such as an itemVariable or choice'); reading 104 as amended: each class's sentence bars its own noun ('any other gap', 'text', 'image', 'hotspot', 'hottext choice'), so no two elements of one class share an identifier, and the four classes' 'any other choice' bars every element the information model calls a choice (§6.17 GapChoice, §5.59, §5.65.1), a gap none (§5.57, gaps filled 'from an associated set of choices'), so a simple, inline, hotspot or simple associable choice shares its identifier with no other choice or hottext of its document, whichever interactions hold them, nor with one its assembly places, compared collapsed; a gap and a gap text may share one (interactions.ts key(on(Choice, "document", "kind", "identifier")), key(on(Hottext, "document", "identifier")) and their placed keys, and queries.ts key(on(ChoiceSpaceName, "document", "identifier")) and key(on(PlacedChoiceSpaceName, "assembly", "identifier")))

entry.name: Href form
entry.source: reading 102 (overlays/package.ts Limit): every href is resolved before its row is written, its value read by its whitespace class, its path merged with the xml:base in scope or its document's path, its dot segments removed and each segment percent-decoded (RFC 3986 §2.1, §5.2 and §6.2.2.2); a path with a scheme, a leading /, a climb above the package root or an external base is external (reading 35), admitted and never resolved where a cp:file or a content reference holds it, and refused where a law needs the href to name an entry; an empty path names its own document (§4.4). What stays refused is a stated limit of the representation, not a law of the specification: a % that starts no percent-encoding, octets that spell no UTF-8, a segment that decodes to / or U+0000, a backslash, a tab, line feed or carriage return a preserving type keeps, and a : in the first segment of a path with no scheme; a srcset's image candidates are each read by its URL, as any href (HTML, 'parse a srcset attribute')

entry.name: Manifest overlay
entry.source: plan §1.6 and the W5 amendment's C18, under decision S3: each manifest overlay (ResourceHref, File) is its element's row, keyed by its node, and holds its own facts alone: it stands at a node of its kind (a constant pin) exactly where its href is written and holds its resolution, never its form, each header with exactly the arm its scope names (grizzle's alternatives: ResourceHrefPath and FilePath an entry path in the package, ResourceHrefOutside and FileOutside a path outside it, as written), and a file's resource is its node's parent, which its laws read through Node; the manifest's identifier is its attribute's value (overlay-queries/package.ts manifestIdentifiers), one per package by the single root N5 admits (Q5.06)

entry.name: Choice identifier key
entry.source: reading 104: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#DataCharacteristic_SimpleChoice.Attr_identifier (§5.132.1, and §5.7.1, §5.55.1, §5.56.1, §5.58.1, §5.65.1, §5.67.1, §5.73.1 and §5.131.1: 'This identifier must not be used by any other choice or item variable', five classes naming their own noun) and https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Derived_Identifier (§7.16: an identifier is 'a logical reference to another object in the item, such as an itemVariable or choice'); reading 104 as amended: each class's sentence bars its own noun ('any other gap', 'text', 'image', 'hotspot', 'hottext choice'), so no two elements of one class share an identifier, and the four classes' 'any other choice' bars every element the information model calls a choice (§6.17 GapChoice, §5.59, §5.65.1), a gap none (§5.57, gaps filled 'from an associated set of choices'), so a simple, inline, hotspot or simple associable choice shares its identifier with no other choice or hottext of its document, whichever interactions hold them, nor with one its assembly places, compared collapsed; a gap and a gap text may share one (interactions.ts key(on(Choice, "document", "kind", "identifier")), key(on(Hottext, "document", "identifier")) and their placed keys, and queries.ts key(on(ChoiceSpaceName, "document", "identifier")) and key(on(PlacedChoiceSpaceName, "assembly", "identifier")))

entry.name: Idref target
entry.source: XML Schema Part 1, Validation Rule: Validation Root (the ID/IDREF table): an IDREF names an ID of its document, an attribute's tokens and an IDREF- or IDREFS-typed element text's alike (§3.15.5; reading 101); reading 14; reading 2 and https://www.w3.org/TR/MathML3/chapter4.html#contm.share (MathML 3 §4.2.7: a share's src names 'the id attribute of the root node of the expression tree' it stands for): a same-document fragment of an m:share's src, a # and the characters after it, names an ID of its document as an IDREF token does, and a src that is no fragment is reading 103's file reference, which is not read here (operator decision 321); and reading 115: an assembly holding an external include merges a resource never fetched (https://www.w3.org/TR/xinclude/#processing, XInclude 1.0 Second Edition §4: the result 'merges the source infoset with the infosets of resources identified by URI references'), whose IDs its IDREFs may name, so its IDREFs are admitted unjudged and its include is named by UnplacedInclude (https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/conf §3: 'ignore or remove the unsupported data')

entry.name: Include root
entry.source: reading 114: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Imported_Include (§9.4.1, Include's parent classes, and 'This denotes the use of the XInclude feature [XInclude, 16]'), https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#AbstractAttribute_FlowGroup_include (§6.15.8 and its siblings: 'This provides the insertion of markup from external files') and https://www.w3.org/TR/xinclude-11/#docii (XInclude 1.1 §4.2.1: an included document's 'set of top-level included items is the children of the acquired infoset's document information item'): an include under a parent whose model holds one stands for its fragment's root, which is one of its particle's choice-group alternatives, a kind whose position the parent's automaton follows and ends on as the include's, and readings 116 and 117: https://www.w3.org/TR/xinclude/#processing (XInclude 1.0 Second Edition §4: the result infoset 'merges the source infoset with the infosets of resources identified by URI references'), so a fragment rooted at a kind the composition splits by context, whose split kind alone the parent admits there, is valid once merged, and is admitted and named by UnplacedInclude (https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/conf §3: 'ignore or remove the unsupported data'), since its root is read by its name alone

entry.name: Test overlay
entry.source: plan §1.7 O7 and the W5 amendment's C15, C18, under decision S3: each O7 overlay (AssembledDocument, Named, Site) is its element's row, keyed by its node, and holds its attributes' values, collapsed, each an identifier read where it stands (TestIdentifier, C18); AssembledDocument and Named hold no fact of their node or document, which their laws read through Node and Document (a document's root kind its Document's, at its (package, path)), while a Site holds its node's context (nodeContext: its kind, parent and parent's kind, ancestry, children, governor and nearest interaction), the copy routed with Document's context to the RULEREC follow-up; each exists exactly where its element does (Q5.13)

entry.name: Idref target
entry.source: XML Schema Part 1, Validation Rule: Validation Root (the ID/IDREF table): an IDREF names an ID of its document, an attribute's tokens and an IDREF- or IDREFS-typed element text's alike (§3.15.5; reading 101); reading 14; reading 2 and https://www.w3.org/TR/MathML3/chapter4.html#contm.share (MathML 3 §4.2.7: a share's src names 'the id attribute of the root node of the expression tree' it stands for): a same-document fragment of an m:share's src, a # and the characters after it, names an ID of its document as an IDREF token does, and a src that is no fragment is reading 103's file reference, which is not read here (operator decision 321); and reading 115: an assembly holding an external include merges a resource never fetched (https://www.w3.org/TR/xinclude/#processing, XInclude 1.0 Second Edition §4: the result 'merges the source infoset with the infosets of resources identified by URI references'), whose IDs its IDREFs may name, so its IDREFs are admitted unjudged and its include is named by UnplacedInclude (https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/conf §3: 'ignore or remove the unsupported data')

entry.source: plan §1.7 O7 and the W5 amendment's C15, C18, under decision S3: each O7 overlay (AssembledDocument, Named, Site) is its element's row, keyed by its node, and holds its attributes' values, collapsed, each an identifier read where it stands (TestIdentifier, C18); AssembledDocument and Named hold no fact of their node or document, which their laws read through Node and Document (a document's root kind its Document's, at its (package, path)), while a Site holds its node's context (nodeContext: its kind, parent and parent's kind, ancestry, children, governor and nearest interaction), the copy routed with Document's context to the RULEREC follow-up; each exists exactly where its element does (Q5.13)

entry.name: Section ref target
entry.source: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Derived_AssessmentSectionRef (§7.5: 'The only documents that can be refered to by qti-assessment-section-ref are XML documents that contain a single qti-assessment-section as a single root'; §7.5.3, the href 'is used to refer to the qti-assessment-section document file e.g. elsewhere in the same content package'): a section ref whose href stays in the package names a listed document there, whose root is a section, which it places in its test's assembly (tests.ts sectionRefSites, SiteTarget); one whose href resolves outside the package is stored as written and never fetched (reading 115), and its test is no deliverable one

entry.name: Include target
entry.source: reading 115: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Imported_Include (§9.4.1: 'This denotes the use of the XInclude feature [XInclude, 16]'); https://www.w3.org/TR/xinclude/#include_element (XInclude 1.0 Second Edition §3.1: 'If the href attribute is absent when parse="xml", the xpointer attribute must be present'; an include that writes an xpointer, or parse="text", is no site, stored as written and never included, reading 85), https://www.w3.org/TR/xinclude/#xml-included-items (§4.2: 'Resources that are unavailable for any reason … result in a resource error', one 'determined through implementation-specific mechanisms not to be XML' among them) and https://www.w3.org/TR/xinclude/#fallback_element (§3.2: 'When a resource error is encountered, the xi:include element is replaced with the contents of the xi:fallback element' and 'If the xi:fallback element is missing, a resource error results in a fatal error'): an include the information model reads names, by an href this representation resolves, a document its package lists, or holds a fallback, which replaces it where its href names an entry that is no document; such an include, and one whose href is external (reading 102), a resource the package does not hold, stored as written and never fetched, is admitted and named by UnplacedInclude (https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/conf §3: an application 'must be able to ignore or remove the unsupported data')

entry.name: Href form
entry.source: reading 102 (overlays/package.ts Limit): every href is resolved before its row is written, its value read by its whitespace class, its path merged with the xml:base in scope or its document's path, its dot segments removed and each segment percent-decoded (RFC 3986 §2.1, §5.2 and §6.2.2.2); a path with a scheme, a leading /, a climb above the package root or an external base is external (reading 35), admitted and never resolved where a cp:file or a content reference holds it, and refused where a law needs the href to name an entry; an empty path names its own document (§4.4). What stays refused is a stated limit of the representation, not a law of the specification: a % that starts no percent-encoding, octets that spell no UTF-8, a segment that decodes to / or U+0000, a backslash, a tab, line feed or carriage return a preserving type keeps, and a : in the first segment of a path with no scheme; a srcset's image candidates are each read by its URL, as any href (HTML, 'parse a srcset attribute')

entry.source: XML Schema Part 1, Validation Rule: Validation Root (the ID/IDREF table): an IDREF names an ID of its document, an attribute's tokens and an IDREF- or IDREFS-typed element text's alike (§3.15.5; reading 101); reading 14; reading 2 and https://www.w3.org/TR/MathML3/chapter4.html#contm.share (MathML 3 §4.2.7: a share's src names 'the id attribute of the root node of the expression tree' it stands for): a same-document fragment of an m:share's src, a # and the characters after it, names an ID of its document as an IDREF token does, and a src that is no fragment is reading 103's file reference, which is not read here (operator decision 321); and reading 115: an assembly holding an external include merges a resource never fetched (https://www.w3.org/TR/xinclude/#processing, XInclude 1.0 Second Edition §4: the result 'merges the source infoset with the infosets of resources identified by URI references'), whose IDs its IDREFs may name, so its IDREFs are admitted unjudged and its include is named by UnplacedInclude (https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/conf §3: 'ignore or remove the unsupported data')

entry.name: Href form
entry.source: reading 102 (overlays/package.ts Limit): every href is resolved before its row is written, its value read by its whitespace class, its path merged with the xml:base in scope or its document's path, its dot segments removed and each segment percent-decoded (RFC 3986 §2.1, §5.2 and §6.2.2.2); a path with a scheme, a leading /, a climb above the package root or an external base is external (reading 35), admitted and never resolved where a cp:file or a content reference holds it, and refused where a law needs the href to name an entry; an empty path names its own document (§4.4). What stays refused is a stated limit of the representation, not a law of the specification: a % that starts no percent-encoding, octets that spell no UTF-8, a segment that decodes to / or U+0000, a backslash, a tab, line feed or carriage return a preserving type keeps, and a : in the first segment of a path with no scheme; a srcset's image candidates are each read by its URL, as any href (HTML, 'parse a srcset attribute')

entry.name: Key text bound
entry.source: src/qti/limits.ts: no index orders by a name, a prefix or a path (the host orders them), and each bound on a text a query reads is PostgreSQL's: a text a query reads by a pattern (matchedText) at most matchedTextBytes UTF-8 bytes, the regex engine's (regexTextMaxBytes); a foreign element's namespace name and local name at most foreignNameBytes each, half of what that engine reads of the expanded name a query matches them as (OpenElementName.expanded), since XML puts no bound on a name (reading 94); and an ARIA bound of a pair that is an xs:decimal at most parsedDecimalBytes, what Text.parseDecimal reads (decimalTextMaxBytes), past which a decimal may name a value numeric does not hold (overlay-queries/interaction.ts Key_text_bound over AriaBounds); a stated limit of the representation, not a law of the specification

entry.source: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#RootCharacteristic_OutcomeDeclaration.Attr_base-type (§4.5.3, and §5.34.3, §5.115.3, §5.151.3: 'The value space from which the variable's value can be drawn (or in the case of containers, from which the individual values are drawn) is identified with a base-type', 'Variables with record cardinality have no base-type'): a record declares no base type (no DeclarationBaseType beside its DeclarationCardinality, a rule over their join), and every other variable writes one, each judged from the declaration's DeclarationCardinality where its cardinality spells a code; a base-type written but spelling nothing is its value domain's alone (spec reading 158)

entry.name: Reserved type
entry.source: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#RootAttribute_AssessmentItem_qti-context-declaration (§4.1.10, and §4.4.7 of a test: 'An implementation MUST support the global variable "QTI_CONTEXT" with record cardinality') and https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Data_ContextDeclaration (§5.34: 'There is one built-in context variable named "QTI_CONTEXT" with record cardinality'), which the implementation guide, a document with no normative mark, declares explicitly (its §3.7.11, 'an explicit (though unnecessary) <qti-context-declaration> of QTI_CONTEXT'): a declaration of QTI_CONTEXT is a record context declaration, since one of another kind or cardinality would make one identifier name two variables (reading 74). SCORE, MAXSCORE and PASSED are typed by no normative rule: §4.5's 'SCORE needs to be a float', 'MAXSCORE needs to be a float' and 'PASSED needs to be a boolean' use no RFC 2119 keyword (§1.3 Conventions), §2.2.2.3's 'MUST' is in a section marked NOT NORMATIVE, and no XSD particle or Schematron rule types them, so a declaration of any type is admitted (J1; the lead's ruling, 2026-11-20)

entry.name: Reserved type
entry.source: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#RootAttribute_AssessmentItem_qti-context-declaration (§4.1.10, and §4.4.7 of a test: 'An implementation MUST support the global variable "QTI_CONTEXT" with record cardinality') and https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Data_ContextDeclaration (§5.34: 'There is one built-in context variable named "QTI_CONTEXT" with record cardinality'), which the implementation guide, a document with no normative mark, declares explicitly (its §3.7.11, 'an explicit (though unnecessary) <qti-context-declaration> of QTI_CONTEXT'): a declaration of QTI_CONTEXT is a record context declaration, since one of another kind or cardinality would make one identifier name two variables (reading 74). SCORE, MAXSCORE and PASSED are typed by no normative rule: §4.5's 'SCORE needs to be a float', 'MAXSCORE needs to be a float' and 'PASSED needs to be a boolean' use no RFC 2119 keyword (§1.3 Conventions), §2.2.2.3's 'MUST' is in a section marked NOT NORMATIVE, and no XSD particle or Schematron rule types them, so a declaration of any type is admitted (J1; the lead's ruling, 2026-11-20)

entry.name: Test overlay
entry.source: plan §1.7 O7 and the W5 amendment's C15, C18, under decision S3: each O7 overlay (AssembledDocument, Named, Site) is its element's row, keyed by its node, and holds its attributes' values, collapsed, each an identifier read where it stands (TestIdentifier, C18); AssembledDocument and Named hold no fact of their node or document, which their laws read through Node and Document (a document's root kind its Document's, at its (package, path)), while a Site holds its node's context (nodeContext: its kind, parent and parent's kind, ancestry, children, governor and nearest interaction), the copy routed with Document's context to the RULEREC follow-up; each exists exactly where its element does (Q5.13)

entry.name: Quotation punctuation
entry.source: reading 127: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Data_Q (§5.111, Q: 'Quotation punctuation (such as quotation marks) that is quoting the contents of the tag must not appear immediately before, after, or inside q tags; they will be inserted into the rendering by the user agent'; ~/.cache/qti-pie/anyuri-specs/qti/info.txt:38355, and the 3.0.1 model's ~/.cache/qti-pie/qti301/info301.txt:39222): a q is refused where the last character of its sibling before it, the first of its sibling after it, or the first or last character of its own content is a quotation mark, one of " « » ‘ ‚ ‛ “ ” „ ‟ ‹ › (main's set, which leaves out the apostrophes ' and ’), each read off a text, whitespace or entity reference row, so an element, a comment or an instruction beside the q holds no punctuation (quotation.ts Quotation_punctuation)

entry.source: plan §1.7 O7 and the W5 amendment's C15, C18, under decision S3: each O7 overlay (AssembledDocument, Named, Site) is its element's row, keyed by its node, and holds its attributes' values, collapsed, each an identifier read where it stands (TestIdentifier, C18); AssembledDocument and Named hold no fact of their node or document, which their laws read through Node and Document (a document's root kind its Document's, at its (package, path)), while a Site holds its node's context (nodeContext: its kind, parent and parent's kind, ancestry, children, governor and nearest interaction), the copy routed with Document's context to the RULEREC follow-up; each exists exactly where its element does (Q5.13)

entry.name: Key text bound
entry.source: src/qti/limits.ts: no index orders by a name, a prefix or a path (the host orders them), and each bound on a text a query reads is PostgreSQL's: a text a query reads by a pattern (matchedText) at most matchedTextBytes UTF-8 bytes, the regex engine's (regexTextMaxBytes); a foreign element's namespace name and local name at most foreignNameBytes each, half of what that engine reads of the expanded name a query matches them as (OpenElementName.expanded), since XML puts no bound on a name (reading 94); and an ARIA bound of a pair that is an xs:decimal at most parsedDecimalBytes, what Text.parseDecimal reads (decimalTextMaxBytes), past which a decimal may name a value numeric does not hold (overlay-queries/interaction.ts Key_text_bound over AriaBounds); a stated limit of the representation, not a law of the specification

entry.name: Prefixed reference
entry.source: readings 48, 86, 88, 106, 107, 110 and 112: https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/qti/v3p0/info#Derived_Variable (§7.47: 'During outcomes processing, values taken from an individual item session can be looked up by prefixing the name of the item variable with the identifier assigned to the item in the qti-assessment-item-ref, separated by a period character'; for an item 'allowed to be replaced (i.e. that have the with-replacement attribute set to "true")', 'a number that denotes the instance's place in the sequence of the item's instantiation is inserted between the item variable identifier and the item variable'), §2.8.5 (a part's or a section's duration 'prefixed with the identifier of the part or section followed by the period character') and §4.2.1 ('Identifiers containing the period character are reserved for use in prefixing'), read over the assembled test (reading 5): a reference placed in a test is accepted only when exactly one of its readings, unsplit, split at a period or numbered, names a variable of the test or of a scope of its assembly, each placement of a scope a reading of its own (reading 86), a setter's identifier unsplit alone (reading 112) (overlay-queries/readings.ts TestReading); the importer states the numbered readings and the readings through an item ref that names no item document, which the database proves and cannot enumerate, since no text operation splits a name at a period in a query (a grizzle ask of 2026-11-20), a name whose only readings are two numbered ones the importer's to tell apart, a recorded under-refusal
